children.text: The reference to the Shadow Fold immediately alerts the audience to the concept of a new world, especially when The Darkling explains that it tore the country in two. Our world has not been torn apart by a magical shadow world.
Alina's hands glowing signifies her powers, immediately informing the audience that this is a world of magic, and it is completely separate from our world.

Each clip further explores the conflicts going on in the world of Shadow and Bone, including military clashes, magical battles, and the knife fights amidst the darkness of the Shadow Fold. Each sequence helps to further build the complex political landscape within Shadow and Bone, and the realm of Ravka.
Leigh Bardugo (the author of
Shadow and Bone)

talks about the creation of the show, and how it collected her multiverse of characters, and implemented plot-lines from each story. The show represented the Grishaverse, which was Leigh's story world for
Six of Crows
and
Shadow and Bone
. Through the show, she was able to have the characters interact early on, which would help set up a crossover in future seasons.

Bardugo talks about the influences for the architecture of the world, as well as the monarchy that rules Ravka. The show also reflects the potential for civil war between the Bolsheviks and the Proletariats, through the First and Second Army. The Second Army is full of Grisha, who are beings able to manipulate matter. The First Army are regular foot soldiers. The Second Army receives better supplies and rations, and more equipment, as they are deemed more valuable (therefore a metaphor for the Bolsheviks).

A book set in another world doesn't necessarily mean it is free of commentary from the existing world. Often times, the otherworld tends to reflect the real world at the reader through a lens of social commentary.
The conflicts between Ravka, Fjerda and Shu Han are lightly inspired by the conflicts between Russia, Europe and Asia during World War II.

The reference to the First Army as cannon fodder is accurate. They are sent through the Shadow Fold as they are viewed as expendable. They are the most replaceable, but Grisha are very powerful and few, and must be protected.

The closeness between Mal and Alina tethers Alina to her humanity when she discovers she has magical powers. It means she is fighting to protect the people she cared for, instead of just losing herself to the corruption of her own power. She fights back against the people that want to use her power, and protects the otherworld.

The Second Army are viewed as more valuable than the First Army, because of Ravka's failure to industrialise. They haven't been able to continue building weaponry, so their only advantage is the magical powers possessed by the Grisha. The Grisha are powerful, and therefore they are hunted by the Fjerdans, who have the Grisha executed upon capture. The Fjerdans are also raised to believe that the Grisha are evil, and should be hunted and killed. They basically believe that Grisha feed on children to survive.
The three orders of the Grisha are each invaluable in a fight.

Summoners can control the elements, like wind, fire, air, water. They are typically employed in hand-to-hand combat, because they are able to fight well, and can use their powers to incapacitate multiple soldiers at once.
The Materialki are able to manipulate objects. This makes them good at inventing things, or constructing armour and other things. They design things to aid the Second Army.

The Heartrenders are their healers, but they can also be deadly on the battlefield. They are able to manipulate a person's body, so they could compress your lungs, or break your bones, but they could also realign them and heal you. They are able to save lives or end them, and they are very dangerous.

General Kirigan is the leader of the Second Army, because he is considered the most powerful of the Grisha. They believe he has the best chance of tearing down the Shadow Fold, and he has promised he will attempt to do just that.

In a way, General Kirigan has more influence over the Second Army than the King himself, purely because the Grisha trust him more. He has protected and defended them as much as he could, and earned them a safe place within Ravka. It makes him a very powerful, very dangerous man.

The Shadow Fold is a threat to the First and Second Armies, because in order to maintain supplies on the front lines of the war, they must traverse the Shadow Fold. If they are unable to retrieve supplies, or the skiff does not make it through, it means fewer rations, less ammunition, and dwindling chances for survival.

So not only do the Ravkan's have to fend off attacks from Fjerda and Shu Han, they have to fend off attacks from the land they live near, and the Volcra, creatures that were formed entirely from darkness.
The myth of the Sun Summoner is an unproven possibility. She is the only true hope they have of erasing the darkness of the Shadow Fold, and rescuing Ravka's war efforts.

General Kirigan, the Darkling, is unable to tear down the Shadow Fold for a very good reason: "have you ever put out a fire by adding more fire?" Any effort he makes to tear down the Shadow Fold only makes the darkness worse.

Alina's discovery of her magic ignites hope across Ravka, and offers a morale boost to the Second Army, and to the First Army as well. It gives Ravka a fighting chance in the war effort, which is a problem for the rest of the world, so Alina quickly becomes hunted. If she tears down the Shadow Fold, it will mean Ravka has a real chance at winning the war, despite its failure to industrialise.

The Six of Crows are a gang of six individuals that live in Ketterdam (West Ravka, through the Shadow Fold). They undertake heists and other criminal enterprises in order to earn money, and establish themselves as powerful people within the Barrel, the criminal underworld of Ketterdam.

There are a lot of political machinations going on, and a lot of corruption in Ketterdam. The powerful people are used to betraying whoever they have to in order to make their money, and Kaz Brekker has debts to settle with many of them. He is determined to earn his revenge, and make some money along the way.

Kaz, Jesper and Inej are known for their cunning schemes, but at the start of Shadow and Bone, they are only beginning to assert themselves as major players within the criminal underworld. They have to find a way to cement their power and authority, and the best way to do that is to undertake the most impressive heists they can.
That, and if someone double crosses them, they have to ensure they don't get away with it.

The biggest heist is to bring Alina Starkov, the alleged Sun Summoner, to Ketterdam. If they succeed, they will be offered a great deal of money, but the risks are high. They would have to infiltrate the Little Palace, and kidnap the most heavily guarded woman in Ravka. If they can manage to succeed, they will become notorious and renowned.

The incredible intricacies of the world building and the detail put into the storylines really help to establish the otherworld as not just a distorted reflection of the existing world, but as a world that stands independently, with its own political issues, and warfare.
The magic system is also beautifully explored, and all of the details just make the world-building even more immersive.
